headline: Large Energy User Grid Cost Shifting
short_summary: This bill aims to shift electricity infrastructure costs from residential ratepayers to large energy users, primarily data centers, potentially saving residential customers money.
status: Last Action: Governor's Action Deadline 11:59 p.m., May 23, 2026 on 2026-04-22
supporters: Residential consumer advocates, environmental groups, Clean Virginia.
opponents: Data center industry, large industrial energy users, Dominion Energy (with initial resistance to some provisions).
news_headline: Governor amends bills that shift costs onto data centers. Critics say her tweaks weaken them.
news_summary: Governor Spanberger signed and suggested changes to HB 1393 and SB 253, which aim to shift energy costs onto high-load users like data centers to save residential customers money and expand a power line burial program. While some amendments were accepted, critics argue the governor's tweaks weakened the original intent of fully shifting costs, particularly regarding capacity auction prices.

headline: Data Center Water Consumption Reporting
short_summary: This bill requires water utilities to report the total volume of water provided to data centers, increasing transparency on their water usage.
status: Last Action: Acts of Assembly Chapter text (CHAP0896) on 2026-04-13
supporters: Environmental groups, local communities concerned about water resources, transparency advocates, Senator Kannan Srinivasan.
opponents: Data center industry (likely views it as an additional regulatory burden).
news_headline: Four data center bills await governor's signature as Southwest Virginia projects spark debate
news_summary: SB 553, among other data center bills, increases reporting requirements for data center water usage, aiming for transparency. This legislation comes as proposals for new data centers in Southwest Virginia fuel debates over environmental impacts, including water consumption.

headline: Data Center Siting and Noise Limits
short_summary: This bill establishes a permit process for high energy use facilities, requiring site assessments for noise impacts on nearby homes and schools, and allowing localities to assess other environmental impacts.
status: Last Action: Incorporated by Counties, Cities and Towns (HB153-Thomas) (Voice Vote) on 2026-01-23
supporters: Local residents near proposed data center sites, community groups, environmental groups, Delegate Josh Thomas, Senator Danica Roem.
opponents: Data center industry, land developers, economic development agencies.
news_headline: Bills on data center siting and water usage remain unresolved as General Assembly session winds down
news_summary: HB 153, similar to SB 94, requires data center developers to conduct site assessments, including noise studies for nearby homes and schools, and assess impacts on water, agriculture, and historic sites. The bill reflects growing concerns from communities about data center sprawl and its local impacts.
